page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual server instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 8 dedicated physical cores and 8 vCPUs utilizing the x86_64 architecture, driven by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying entirely on external block storage and network-attached resources. Network connectivity is supported by a baseline bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations place the instance's performance largely in the average to weak categories. The Geekbench single-core score of 1315.0 and multi-core score of 5025.0 rank in the middle 50% tier, alongside average results for software compilation (7237.0) and ray tracing (8201.0). However, raw compute benchmarks show limitations, with stress-ng single-core performance scoring 768.28 (bottom 10%) and multi-core scoring 3073.97 (bottom 25%). Memory performance is mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is average at 395.92 GB/sec, large-block uncached read and write bandwidths fall into the bottom 25% tier at 32.16 GB/sec and 16.75 GB/sec, respectively.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c6a.2xlarge offers dedicated AMD EPYC cores at a lower resource density, making it suitable for workloads that require dedicated CPU allocation without massive memory footprints. Supported by instruction sets like AVX, AES, and SHA_NI, it is well-suited for standard web serving, where it achieves a static web serving throughput of 6.78 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 2659.95 in Passmark database tests. It is also appropriate for Redis deployments, handling 7.44 million SET operations per second, as well as light software compilation and text processing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c6a.2xlarge is an x86_64 compute-optimized instance featuring 8 dedicated vCPUs and 8 physical cores powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz. It is configured with 16.0 GB of RAM (2.0 GB per core), 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, and no local storage or GPU hardware. Performance benchmarks indicate average capabilities across most standard operations, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 5025.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 10249.39. While raw compute benchmarks like stress-ng fall into lower percentiles, the instance maintains average performance in memory bandwidth for small cached blocks and database operations. This instance is qualitatively cost-effective for dedicated compute workloads with moderate memory requirements, making it suitable for static web serving, Redis key-value stores, and light database operations.
